chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the man who has not yet performed Hajj (Sarurat), performing Hajj on behalf of the deceased. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if the Sarurat does not have what he can perform Hajj with for himself. But if he has what he can perform Hajj with for himself, then it is not sufficient for him until he performs Hajj from his own wealth. And it is sufficient on behalf of the deceased, whether the Sarurat has wealth or if he does not have wealth.'

key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: A person who dies without having performed the obligatory Hajj
key_terms.يَحُجُّ عَنِ الْمَيِّتِ: Performing Hajj on behalf of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Hajj for a deceased person who died without having performed their obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the priority of Hajj al-Din (Hajj of obligation) in estate distribution, distinguishing between a deceased who had wealth but neglected the ritual versus one who lacked means. It establishes that if the deceased possessed sufficient funds, the heirs must first perform Hajj from his estate before settling debts or bequests, ensuring the religious duty is fulfilled from his own assets. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that Hajj is a debt upon the soul, prioritized over general inheritance claims when the deceased had the capacity to perform it.
